sentences.ko: 아, 살면서 이렇게 불편했던 적은 처음이야.
sentences.text: Oh, I have never been so uncomfortable in my entire life.

alts.text: That was the most awkward thing ever.
I do not think I have ever felt this uncomfortable before.

sentences.note: **so uncomfortable**은 몸이 불편한 것뿐 아니라 분위기가 어색해서 가시방석일 때도 씁니다. **in my entire life**를 붙이면 '살다 살다 이런 건 처음'이라는 과장이 됩니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 8 | Friends

sentences.ko: 근데 반바지 입기엔 밖이 좀 춥지 않아?
sentences.text: So, isn't it a bit cold out for shorts?

alts.text: Kinda chilly for shorts, no?
Is it not rather cold outside to be wearing shorts?

sentences.note: **cold out**의 out은 '바깥 날씨'라는 뜻이라 outside를 다 말하지 않아도 됩니다. **a bit**을 넣으면 상대 옷차림을 지적할 때 말이 부드러워집니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 아 진짜, 내가 이걸 고민하고 있다니 말도 안 돼.
sentences.text: Oh god, I can't believe I'm even considering this.

alts.text: Can't believe I'm actually thinking about this.
I cannot believe that I am even considering this.

sentences.note: **even considering**은 '하는 것도 아니고 고민하는 것만으로도' 어이없다는 느낌입니다. 평소라면 안 할 일에 마음이 흔들릴 때 스스로에게 하는 말로 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 전화 요금 고지서가 와도 바로 내진 않잖아.
sentences.text: The phone bill arrives, but you don't pay it right away.

alts.text: You get the phone bill and just let it sit.
When the telephone bill comes, you do not pay it immediately.

sentences.note: **right away**는 '바로, 당장'으로 일상에서 immediately보다 훨씬 자주 씁니다. **let it sit**은 처리할 것을 그냥 놔둘 때 쓰는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 드디어 우리가 이걸 하게 돼서 정말 좋다.
sentences.text: And I'm so glad we're finally doing this.

alts.text: Finally! Glad we're doing this.
I am very pleased that we are at last doing this.

sentences.note: **finally doing this**는 몇 번 미루던 약속이나 계획을 드디어 할 때 씁니다. 오랜만에 모인 자리에서 건배하듯 꺼내기 좋은 말입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 제발 내가 골라 주는 거 그냥 입어. 그러면 그 여자가 너한테 완전 반할 거야.
sentences.text: Please just wear what I suggest and she is going to go nuts for you.

alts.text: Trust me, wear what I pick. She'll go crazy for you.
I would ask that you simply wear what I recommend; she will be very taken with you.

sentences.note: **go nuts for**는 누군가에게 완전히 빠지거나 열광한다는 뜻이에요. 사람뿐 아니라 음식이나 물건에도 써요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 근데 우리 부모님은 그때쯤엔 '어, 그래, 뭐 새삼스럽지도 않네' 하는 식이었어.
sentences.text: But to my parents, by then it was like, yeah, right, well, what else is new?

alts.text: My parents? By then they were just like, eh, nothing new.
However, by that point, my parents' reaction was essentially, 'Of course. That is nothing new.'

sentences.note: **what else is new?**는 '늘 그렇지 뭐', '새삼스럽지도 않다'는 뜻으로, 또 그 일이냐며 시큰둥하게 받을 때 써요. **it was like**는 그때의 반응이나 분위기를 흉내 낼 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 왜 거길 찾아볼 생각을 못 했는지 모르겠네.
sentences.text: I don't know why we didn't think to check there.

alts.text: Can't believe we never checked there.
I do not understand why it did not occur to us to look there.

sentences.note: **didn't think to**는 '~할 생각을 못 했다'는 뜻이에요. 뻔한 곳에서 물건을 찾았을 때처럼 놓친 걸 뒤늦게 깨달았을 때 써요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 설마 우리 할머니가 돌아가시기 전에 절대 집안 밖으로 내보내지 말라고 맹세까지 시킨 그거 말하는 거야?
sentences.text: You mean the one that my grandmother made me swear on her deathbed that I would never let out of our family?

alts.text: Wait, Grandma's thing? The one I swore I'd never give away?
Are you referring to the one my grandmother made me promise, on her deathbed, never to let outside our family?

sentences.note: **You mean the one**은 상대가 말한 게 그게 맞는지 되물을 때 써요. **swear on her deathbed**는 임종 자리에서 맹세했다는 뜻으로, 꼭 지켜야 하는 약속을 말할 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 이제 옆을 돌아봤을 때 거기 누가 있겠냐고.
sentences.text: And now when I look over, who am I going to see?

alts.text: Who's gonna be there when I turn around now?
Who will I see beside me from now on when I turn my head?

sentences.note: **look over**는 고개를 돌려 옆이나 건너편을 본다는 뜻이에요. 늘 곁에 있던 사람이 떠날 때 아쉬움을 담아 이렇게 말해요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends
